title: 3.7.5 Plain English to Pseudocode: What `.map()` Does for You
description: Turn four plain-English steps into pseudocode for what .map() does: a loop you did not write, one result per item, collected in a new list.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([Start]) --> B[start an empty list]
  B --> C{{go through the prices}}
  C --> D{is there another price?}
  D -- yes --> E[add the taxed price to the list]
  E --> C
  D -- no --> F[/show the list/]
  F --> Z([End])
planChart.caption: map as a loop: the yes branch adds one taxed price and goes back to the loop setup, and only the no branch reaches the print.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Start with an empty list called `withTax`.

**2.** Go through the prices one at a time.

**3.** For each price, multiply it by 1.08 and add the result to `withTax`.

**4.** When there are no more prices, print `withTax`.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor (open the Flow Chart bar). You do not draw it, you read it: the loop is the hexagon and the diamond, and `FOR EACH` does both jobs, so the diamond has no line of its own.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Your four steps take **five** lines, because END FOR is a line too. Number every line, including the indented line and the END FOR line (not the END at the bottom of the editor). Indent the line inside the loop. The loop is always `FOR EACH` here, even where earlier JavaScript used an index. Write multiplying with `*`. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `SET greeting TO "Hello"` (a change)
- `FOR EACH name IN names` ... `END FOR` (the loop)
- `ADD name TO roster` (a step inside the loop)
- `SET area TO width * height` (multiply with `*`)
- `OUTPUT roster` or `RETURN roster` (the answer, after the loop)

Before you submit, trace `prices` holding `[10, 20, 30]` by hand: three passes, three entries added, and the answer shown once.
hints: The loop is `FOR EACH ... END FOR`, and the steps inside it are indented.
Whatever happens once the loop is over comes after END FOR, not inside it.

requirements.title: Five numbered steps in a row
requirements.description: Number every step 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: You need at least five lines that start with a number, one after another, each with a step written after it. Number END FOR and the indented line too.

requirements.title: The list starts empty, before the loop
requirements.description: withTax is started as an empty list, before the loop begins.
requirements.hint: Start the list once, before the loop, for example SET names TO an empty list, using your own name for it. Do not start it again inside the loop.

requirements.title: One loop over prices, closed
requirements.description: Exactly one loop over prices, closed with END FOR.
requirements.hint: Use one FOR EACH over prices, close it with one END FOR, and number both lines.

requirements.title: The taxed price is added inside the loop
requirements.description: Each pass adds the taxed price to withTax.
requirements.hint: Inside the loop, multiply the price by 1.08 and add that result to withTax, using the same name you gave the loop. Each pass adds one entry.

requirements.title: The answer comes after the loop
requirements.description: withTax is shown once the loop is over.
requirements.hint: Show or return withTax after END FOR, on the path taken once there are no more prices.

requirements.title: Nothing is shown inside the loop
requirements.description: The answer comes after END FOR, not between FOR EACH and END FOR.
requirements.hint: Either there is no FOR EACH loop yet, or a step inside it prints or returns. The answer is shown once, after END FOR.
